analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (Qwen27 native context, media ingress, assistant and cluster text; the Gemma TP placement text is only visible in the patch excerpt) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. No executable code, so no direct regression. The security-relevant item is the new 'Gemma TP prompt prefixes' section (prefix-cache.md patch hunk @@ -1260, head lines ~1267-1320). It describes a new cache surface under the T-041 / TB-007 family: Gemma 4 tensor parallel adds a resident memory tier (QwenStagePrefixCache) and an encrypted SSD tier (QwenStagePrefixDiskTier) keyed by Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes, 'in the request's tenant partition'. The doc also says tiers reuse the cluster family SSD config (key, owner-only directories, TTL, daily write cap, free-space floor). Claims to verify in code review: (1) the tenant partition / cacheSalt is folded into both resident and SSD scopes (T-041 mitigation d); (2) on-disk names use HMAC lookup tags and carry no raw token-prefix hash (leak #2); (3) the 30-minute TTL cap and KEK-wipe purge apply to this tier; (4) the restore path writes into reserved pages with reservedTokens and releases rows on failure; (5) the vote and confirm exchange is sealed, the same on both ranks, and a mismatch causes both ranks to prefill from zero. The doc states the SSD scope excludes the membership epoch and includes the storage commitment and artifact, which looks consistent with the T-041 posture. The doc says nothing explicit about default-on state beyond the load agreement 'on' with the kill switch DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=off. T-041's affected_files list does not include the cluster stage prefix tiers, so the threat model may need updating to cover the Gemma TP prefix cache and the same-account TTFT oracle across ranks. No code evidence is supplied, so this is recorded as an integration question and not a finding. The inference.md excerpts describe memory accounting and arithmetic-equality claims (no new trust boundary).
